author: cens0r3d
install_msg:
Thank you for installing KickAlerts!

Setup: this cog talks to the external Kick.com API (api.kick.com/public/v1) and needs OAuth2 app credentials. Create them at https://kick.com/settings/developer, then either run `[p]kickalert setcreds <client_id> <client_secret>` (bot owner, the message is deleted again) or store them in Red's shared token store with `[p]set api kick client_id,<id> client_secret,<secret>`. `[p]kickalert authstatus` verifies them.

Then pick an alert channel with `[p]kickalert setchannel #channel` and add streamers with `[p]kickalert add <username> [channel]`. Alerts announce a stream when it goes live, keep the embed updated while it runs, and turn into a stream-ended message (or get deleted) when it stops.

Data: the credentials live in Red's shared API tokens, everything else (channel and role IDs, per-streamer settings, custom messages, the last known live state) in Red's Config. No message content and nothing about individual users is stored.
name: KickAlerts
short: Kick.com livestream announcements using the official Kick public API.
description: Monitor Kick.com streamers through the official public API (api.kick.com/public/v1) with OAuth2 app credentials. Announces streams when they go live, refreshes the alert while the stream runs, and reports the stream end with its duration. Includes per-streamer channels, ping roles and custom messages with placeholders, viewer/category visibility, minimal or detailed embeds, per-guild poll intervals, pausing per streamer or per server, and a polling loop that retries rate limits and keeps working through API errors.
end_user_data_statement: This cog stores guild-level configuration (alert channel and role IDs, poll interval, embed settings, per-streamer settings and the last known live state) in Red's Config, and the Kick API credentials in Red's shared API token store. No message content and no per-user data is stored.
